items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It’s got this thing with Paul Chambers and the tuba... They did this in the original Porgy and Bess... Gil Evans.

ctx.x: You feel it. Then if you write the tuba and the bass together, you got something fantastic, because the tuba is not built to be played real loud, especially in the upper register. It’s built to be played soft up there. Then it can be controlled and it can be beautiful. If you write up there with the bass, the tuba, you don’t need anything else playing. You can take the drummer out. You can take the piano player out. You can fire everybody. Just let those two guys play. It’s in The Buzzard Song, I think it is,…
They did this in the original Porgy and Bess, but they didn’t do it like that. They didn’t do that. Gil Evans.
